FDA suspends licences of nine Mumbai restaurants, including Naturals, Bayroute, Khala Goda’s Chetana
 Five persons were arrested for dealing in stocks under a ban like paan masala with a value of ₹1.68 lakh
 Updated - November 19, 2026 04:37 pm IST - Mumbai 
 Chinmay Gaikwad READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 At Naturals Ice Cream in Churchgate, inspectors found ice cream without covers inside a freezer with dirt.
 | Photo Credit: Special arrangement
 The Maharashtra Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) has suspended licenses of nine restaurants in Mumbai, seizing stocks of food with a value of ₹1.27 crore, after inspections showed a lack of compliance with procedures for safety and guidelines for storage.
 The FDA crackdown on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) also led to the licence suspension of 12 restaurants across the State, closing of operations of six vendors, and arrest of five persons for dealing in stocks under a ban like paan masala with a value of ₹1.68 lakh.
 Food and Drug Administration seizes 20,085 litres of oil in Pune over violations of standards The nine Mumbai spots that have had to shut include Gupta Fruit Juice Centre at Nariman Point, Prakash Dosa at Fort, and Saurabh Hotels at Colaba.
 At Naturals Ice Cream in Churchgate, inspectors found ice cream without covers inside a freezer with dirt. The counter with dust and flies was found products without labels for dates of manufacturing or expiry, and also held items like gloves and chargers for phones alongside food.
 A cockroach was found on a menu card at a table in an outlet of Miyan Kababs at Fort. The other violations included - flies on the premises, chicken meat stored without cover in a chiller at 13°C which is above the limit set by standards of below 4°C, containers of gravy on the floor, and a mincer for meat with rust, and residue alongside plates that had undergone washing.
 FDA suspends 105 licences, cancels 7 across Maharashtra after pre-Deepavali checks Meanwhile, the outlet of Bayroute at Cuffe Parade faced action due to the presence of rodents and flies entering through openings without mesh, a smell from three toilets near the room for desserts preparation, and a drain without a cover beneath a rack holding utensils.
 The restaurant Chetana at Kala Ghoda stored food in containers not meant for food on racks with rust, the refrigerator had gaskets with damage, tiles were broken, a ceiling leaked with fungus and soot over the area for washing utensils, and the establishment lacked records for the control of pests and certifications.
 Inspectors found bags of waste containing liquid near the counter for the preparation of food at Cafe Ideal at Radio Club
 | Photo Credit: 
 Special arrangement
 Inspectors found bags of waste containing liquid near the counter for the preparation of food at Cafe Ideal at Radio Club. Among other issues at the facility, cut onions were left without cover near a bin and a sink; soot and paint coming off along with wires without covering on the ceiling of the kitchen; and meat stored without cover.
 The Shreeyog Restaurant at Fort had kept food items on the floor near garbage bins without covers, flies were found in the kitchen as the door at the rear lacked a mesh to stop insects, cooked vegetables remained without cover. The facility lacked a provision for water at a temperature above the norm for sanitizing utensils, and the staff were found to be handling food without gloves.
